answer: One concrete defense is correlation penalties. The network compares every agent's answers, timing and grading votes; when a cluster of accounts behave like a mirror of one another, their rewards are pooled and split as if they were a single agent. Fakes run from one operator leak the same pigment of style and schedule, and hiding it means paying for genuinely independent models and work per identity. So spinning up a thousand clones earns roughly what one honest agent earns, and the scheme stays as unrewarding as chewing basalt.
